summary: The 36% 401-invalid_token failure rate that began as a clean step at 2026-04-15T14:02Z is best explained by the auth-service v7.3.0 release dep-5710 (jjwt 0.11->0.12 parser API break + TokenValidator rewrite) landing at 14:00Z, but this remains below the confidence threshold (top hypothesis 0.48, low). Two auth-service changes landed within 60 seconds of each other and of the onset — dep-5710 at 14:00Z and the signing-key rotation cfg-2705 at 14:01Z — and neither was rolled back, so change history alone cannot attribute the failure. H2 is favored only by symptom shape (fast, in-process failures with flat traffic/latency/CPU/rate-limiting and a stable ~1/3 partial failure), while its decisive hop (the rewritten validator rejecting a deterministic token subset) is inferred, not proven, because auth-service logs are unsearchable (identity-namespace pipeline down). We recommend treating this as a genuine fork: verify the code path first via a canary/rollback test, with the key-id repin (cfg-2705) as the alternate.

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT library upgrade in dep-5710 (jjwt 0.11->0.12, TokenValidator rewrite) regressed validation for a subset of tokens
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deployment dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0) landed at 14:00Z with a breaking jjwt 0.11->0.12 parser API change and a rewritten TokenValidator. The new parser rejects a stable subset of otherwise-valid tokens - e.g. claim/clock-skew default or algorithm handling changed, matching HIST-109's clock-skew regression - producing 401 invalid_token for ~1/3 of validations while traffic, latency and CPU are untouched. Origin: the auth-service code release.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 upgrades jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 with a breaking parser API and a rewritten TokenValidator, deployed 14:00Z, status live, not rolled back [F1,F14,F6].
The rewritten validator changes token acceptance behavior (claim parsing, clock-skew default, or algorithm handling), so a deterministic subset of previously-valid tokens now fails.
Onset of 401s is a clean step from 0.2% to 36-38% between 14:01Z and 14:02Z, two minutes after the deploy, not a ramp [F7,F34].

Failures are fast and in-process: request_rate unchanged (~390-415 req/s), latency_p99 flat ~85-101ms, cpu_pct flat ~38%, no rate limiting - consistent with a validator rejecting tokens without any downstream stall [F9,F10,F11].

Precedent HIST-109 ('Token validation regression after auth library upgrade', root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default') is the exact change type seen here, and produces exactly this partial invalid_token symptom [F5,F17].

assumptions: A code-level validation regression can produce a stable ~36% partial failure rather than a total outage (e.g., only tokens with a particular claim shape, issuer or algorithm).
No rollback occurred, so the regression persists - consistent with the sustained 2h+ error rate.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Signing-key rotation (cfg-2705) left replicas split between old and new key material, causing partial 401 invalid_token
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 14:01Z cfg-2705 rotated jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04. The proposed mechanism is that the new key id was published before all auth-service replicas had loaded/refreshed it, so a stable fraction (~36%) of validations that reference key material a given replica lacks are rejected as invalid_token while the rest succeed. Origin: auth-service signing-key configuration, not the code. Status: the evidence that would have made this mechanism testable does not exist in this toolset, and one direct prediction of it is contradicted.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 flips jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01Z, authored by security-automation as a scheduled rotation, one minute before the 14:02Z onset [F2,F13,F7].
The new key id reaches only some replicas (or is not uniformly published to the JWKS), splitting pods between old and new key material.
Validations landing on replicas without the new key return invalid_token; a stable ~1/3 fail.

Symptom shape fits a partial/fixed-subset failure: request_rate, latency_p99, cpu_pct and rate_limited_per_min are all flat at onset, so failures are fast and not load-driven [F9,F10,F11]; api-gateway absorbs a diluted ~21% [F12].

assumptions: A key-distribution mechanism exists that re-publishes keys to replicas, despite no JWKS/key-distribution/KMS node in the service graph (F20) and no edge by which key material could propagate (F21).
Some replicas would carry the new key and others not, despite auth-service 'restarts' being exactly 0 at every point (F33) - the classic trigger for a replica to be on a stale key set.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External identity provider / JWKS hosting or credential (signing key / KMS) failed outside auth-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service is a victim: the JWKS endpoint or KMS/secret store serving signing keys (possibly in the identity namespace, whose log pipeline is down) failed or rotated inconsistently, so tokens signed with a key auth-service cannot verify are rejected. Origin: the external signing/verification dependency, not auth-service.

causal_chain.claim: Token verification depends on JWKS/signing keys, and the identity namespace is partially unobservable (log pipeline down) [F18].
The key material served to auth-service became inconsistent with the signing keys (a rotation at the source), so a subset of tokens cannot be verified.
~1/3 of validations fail as invalid_token with a stable fraction [F8].
Onset 14:02Z coincides with the identity-namespace change window [F7,F18].

assumptions: An external rotation/misconfiguration occurred but was recorded only as cfg-2705 on auth-service, or was not recorded at all - despite cfg-2705 being the ONLY config change across all services in the window (F2,F13).

There exists an external key-hosting component reachable by auth-service, despite the service graph containing no JWKS/KMS node (F20) and auth-service having no edge to any key-distribution endpoint (F21).
kyc-provider has no telemetry (has_telemetry false), so no direct external evidence exists.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared dependency (redis-cache session/token cache, or user-db) degraded at ~14:00Z, invalidating a third of token checks
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 401 invalid_token failures originate in a shared dependency rather than auth-service itself: redis-cache (shared:true) or user-db. A cache miss/eviction or DB issue at ~14:00Z would make a stable fraction of cached token/session lookups fail, surfacing as invalid_token. Origin: the shared cache/DB component.

causal_chain.claim: auth-service depends on redis-cache (shared:true) and user-db [F4].
redis-cache or user-db degraded or was perturbed around 14:00Z.
A fraction of token/session lookups fail, yielding invalid_token 401s.
Onset at 14:02Z with a stable ~36% fraction [F7,F8].

assumptions: A cache or DB degradation severe enough to fail ~36% of token checks could leave hit_ratio_pct, connected_clients, cpu, connections_active, slow_queries and replication_lag all perfectly flat - a strained assumption.
Any such degradation was unrecorded: no config change or deployment touches redis-cache or user-db in the window (only dep-5699 and dep-5710, and one config change, exist).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Directly measured and refuted by the newly retrieved shared-dependency telemetry. redis-cache hit_ratio_pct is flat and healthy (94.65-97.70, mean 96.01) with no drop at 14:00-14:02Z (F25); redis-cache connected_clients and cpu_pct are flat (F26); user-db connections_active, slow_queries_per_min and replication_lag_ms are all flat across 13:50-14:15Z (F27,F28); F30 summarises that every measured shared-dependency metric is stable at the exact moment 401s began. A degradation producing 36% validation failures cannot coexist with a fully healthy, unstressed cache and DB. The critic's objection that these metrics were never queried is now answered - they were, and they cleared H3.

facts.statement: auth-service error rate jumped from a ~0.2% baseline to ~36% in a clean step between 14:01Z (0.16%) and 14:02Z (36.08%), not a gradual ramp, and stayed sustained at ~35-37% through 15:56Z (2h+).

auth-service request_rate (~390-415 req/s), latency_p99_ms (~85-101 ms), cpu_pct (~34-42%) and rate_limited_per_min (~2/min) were all flat across the onset, so the failures are a fast, in-process fraction of unchanged traffic rather than a load surge, saturation, rate-limiting event or slow dependency stall.
The upstream api-gateway shows the same onset at the 14:00Z bucket but a lower magnitude (~21% vs auth-service 36%), and stays at ~21% through 15:56Z.

Only two auth-service changes exist in the window: dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0, 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation', breaking changes jjwt 0.11->0.12 parser API and TokenValidator rewrite) at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z, and cfg-2705 (jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04, 'Scheduled signing-key rotation', author security-automation) at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z.

cfg-2705's full change record contains only service/key/old_value/new_value/author/description — no indication of a co-published JWKS update, no push-vs-pull mode and no refresh interval; the deployment record carries no key/version metadata either.
auth-service restarts are exactly 0.0 at every data point across 10:00Z-15:55Z (241+ points, missing_points 0), so no auth-service pod restarted around the 14:00-14:05Z onset.

All measured shared-dependency metrics are flat and healthy across 13:50-14:15Z and show no deviation at the 14:00-14:02Z onset: redis-cache hit_ratio_pct 94.65-97.70 (mean 96.01), connected_clients 292.46-331.89, cpu_pct 19.57-23.19%; user-db connections_active 23.53-27.21, slow_queries_per_min 0.17-0.47, replication_lag_ms 28.07-33.0.

auth-service's only shared (shared:true) dependency is redis-cache, which also feeds portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service; none of those services is named in the incident, and the 401 pattern is identity-specific.

auth-service's dependency edges are only user-db (db), redis-cache (cache) and kyc-provider (external); there is no edge to any JWKS/key-distribution/KMS/pub-sub endpoint, and no JWKS or key-distribution component exists in the service graph (jwks-service returns not_found).

No per-replica/per-pod key-consumption record exists anywhere in the returned change/deployment/dependency data, and auth-service exposes only 7 aggregate service-level metrics with no pod dimension and no JWKS/key-cache/key-fetch metric.

The only external dependency of auth-service (kyc-provider) has has_telemetry false and auth-service's owner namespace is 'identity', consistent with the reported identity-namespace log-pipeline outage; no change-set item touches the pipeline.

assumptions: ASSUMPTION: A code-level validation regression (the rewritten TokenValidator under jjwt 0.12) can produce a stable ~36% partial failure rather than a total outage — e.g. only tokens with a particular claim shape, issuer or algorithm are rejected.
ASSUMPTION: No rollback of dep-5710 or cfg-2705 occurred, so whichever change is responsible persists — consistent with the sustained 2h+ error rate.

ASSUMPTION: The uniform ~36% aggregate error rate reflects a uniform behavior across replicas (H2-style), rather than a bimodal per-replica split; this cannot be confirmed because no pod-level metric exists.

ASSUMPTION: Attribution to the code release rests on symptom shape (fast in-process failures) plus the absence of any represented key-distribution path or restart signal, not on direct byte-level proof of validator behavior.
ASSUMPTION: The identity-namespace log-pipeline outage is an independent, unrelated issue (tracked separately) and is not itself part of the change wave that caused the 401s.
ASSUMPTION: The change/deployment records returned are complete for the window (count:1 config change, two deployments across all services), i.e. no unrecorded change occurred.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Neither change was rolled back (dep-5710 status live / rolled_back_at null) and no subsequent auth-service change appears in the window; the two changes are 60 seconds apart, so change history alone cannot attribute the 401s to config vs code.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Because telemetry offers only an aggregate service-level error_rate, the metric layer cannot distinguish a bimodal per-pod split from a uniform ~36% regression — a limit of the data in both directions.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Historical precedents exist for both candidate changes: HIST-108 (2025-10-01, '401s after JWT signing key rotation', root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS') and HIST-109 (2025-07-11, 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade', root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default'); both are leads only, not evidence about the current incident.

timeline.event: Only non-auth deployment in the window: dep-5699 on market-data-service (v5.0.3, 'update ISIN map') lands, ~2.5h before the report.
Deployment dep-5710 lands on auth-service: v7.3.0, 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation', with breaking change jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API) and TokenValidator rewritten.

Config change cfg-2705 on auth-service rotates jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04, authored by security-automation as a 'Scheduled signing-key rotation' — the only config change across all services in the window.
Last clean data point: auth-service error_rate 0.16%.
Onset: auth-service error_rate steps to 36.08% (38.34% at 14:03). Request rate, p99 latency, CPU and rate-limit counters unchanged; redis-cache and user-db metrics unchanged.
Incident INC-007 reported (SEV-1): ~a third of token validations fail with 401 invalid_token; auth-service logs unsearchable due to the identity-namespace log-pipeline outage.
Error rate still sustained and stable at ~35-37% (2h+ after onset), with no rollback of either change; api-gateway error rate ~21% over the same span.

recommended_actions.action: If feasible at this severity, roll back dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0) to the last pre-14:00Z build — equivalently deploy with the previous jjwt/TokenValidator code — and watch auth-service error_rate for 5 minutes. A step back to ~0.2% confirms H2; no change strengthens H1 (cfg-2705).
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 is the top-ranked hypothesis (0.48) and dep-5710 landed 2 minutes before onset with a breaking parser API change and a rewritten TokenValidator. Because neither change was rolled back (F6/F15), a controlled revert is both the mitigation and the decisive discriminator between H1 and H2.

recommended_actions.action: In parallel (do not stack changes without measurement), be ready to repin cfg-2705 jwt.signing.key_id back from k-2026-04 to k-2025-10. Repin only after the dep-5710 rollback is observed, or as the first move if rollback is blocked.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 (0.27) predicts the same 401 invalid_token partial-failure signature from the 14:01Z key rotation; HIST-108 documents exactly this failure mode. The two changes are 60 seconds apart and neither is rolled back (F2/F6/F13/F15), so the alternate fix must be explicit and the two must not be applied simultaneously if attribution is to be preserved.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm and close H4/H3 operationally: verify there is no JWKS/KMS/key-distribution component or external identity-provider alert outstanding, and confirm redis-cache/user-db health is unchanged. Do not spend more query budget on shared-dependency metrics unless the error signature spreads to portfolio-service, pricing-engine or market-data-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: H3 is positively refuted (all redis-cache/user-db metrics flat at onset) and H4 is contradicted (no JWKS/KMS node, no key-distribution edge, no external change recorded), so both should be closed rather than re-investigated.

recommended_actions.action: After a rollback/revert identifies the culprit, verify the fix by confirming auth-service error_rate returns to ~0.2% baseline, api-gateway error rate returns to <0.3%, and the rate stays flat for at least 30 minutes; then close the incident with the identified change id.
recommended_actions.rationale: F7/F8/F12 give a quantified baseline and incident-level signature (auth-service 0.2% -> 36%; gateway <0.3% -> 21%) that provide an unambiguous pass/fail check for the mitigation.

recommended_actions.action: Add the missing discriminators before the next change of this type: per-replica/pod key-id and key-load state, a JWKS/key-cache/key-fetch metric, per-key-id/per-issuer error attribution, and a co-deploy guard so a code release and a signing-key rotation cannot land within the same minute on auth-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: This incident was unresolvable to root cause because the decisive evidence does not exist: no pod-level metric or replica identity (F31/F32/F22), no JWKS/key-fetch metric (F20/F21, F31), no per-key/per-issuer error grouping (F35), and two indistinguishable changes 60 seconds apart (F6/F15).

recommended_actions.action: Restore or work around the identity-namespace log pipeline (separate ticket) so auth-service 401 error text and rejected key id are searchable; until then, ensure auth-service emits key-id/issuer-labelled validation-failure counters directly to a searchable sink.
recommended_actions.rationale: The log pipeline outage left no log evidence of the invalid_token signature, rejected key id, or per-replica onset timing (F18), which is why this incident ends attributive rather than proven.

data_gaps: No per-replica/pod key-consumption or key-load state exists or could be queried, so the decisive H1-vs-H2 discriminator (some replicas on k-2025-10, others on k-2026-04) is unobservable; auth-service exposes only 7 aggregate metrics with no pod dimension and pod-named services return not_found (F22, F31, F32).

auth-service logs are unsearchable because the identity-namespace log pipeline is down (separate ticket), so no 401 error text, rejected key id, or per-replica onset timing could be obtained; onset is inferred from metrics only (F18).

There is no JWKS/key-distribution/KMS node in the service graph (jwks-service returns not_found) and no edge by which key material could propagate to auth-service, so whether k-2026-04 was published and how consumers refresh it (push vs pull, interval) is unanswerable; the config record carries no such fields (F19-F21, F24).
No per-key-id, per-issuer or per-client error breakdown and no per-pod error split exist in the metric set, so the failing subset cannot be attributed to a key, issuer or replica cohort (F35, F31).
The 14:00Z deployment and the 14:01Z key rotation are 60 seconds apart, neither rolled back, with no ordering signal, so change history alone cannot separate code vs config causation (F6, F15).

auth-service replica count and rebuild/restart behavior were not directly observed beyond the restarts metric (which is 0.0 throughout), so no replica cold-start on a stale key set can be confirmed or excluded (F33).

No direct error-rate or latency metric exists for redis-cache or user-db; the H3 clearance rests on healthy proxy metrics (hit ratio, connections, CPU, slow queries, replication lag) rather than on a direct error/latency signal, though those proxy metrics are unambiguous at onset (F25-F30).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Any per-replica/pod evidence that some auth-service replicas were serving under key id k-2025-10 while others used k-2026-04 (or a bimodal per-pod error rate) would move the conclusion to H1 (cfg-2705).

A rollback experiment: if reverting dep-5710 (v7.3.0) does not change the ~36% error rate but repinning cfg-2705 to k-2025-10 does, H1 is confirmed and H2 refuted; the reverse (error rate returns to baseline on code rollback) confirms H2.

auth-service 401 log text or a rejected key-id field showing an algorithm/claim/clock-skew rejection consistent with jjwt 0.12 behavior would raise H2 to proven root cause; 401 text naming a key-id mismatch would instead support H1.
Evidence of an external identity-provider or KMS key-hosting failure or rotation recorded outside auth-service (or an identity-namespace event) would revive H4.

Any recorded auth-service change or deployment between 14:02Z and 15:59Z (e.g. an unrecorded restart, config push, or staged rollout) would reopen the attribution entirely, since the current conclusion relies on the change set being complete.

findings.statement: Neither the v7.3.0 deployment nor the key rotation was rolled back: the deployment still shows status 'live'/'rolled_back_at':null, and no subsequent auth-service config change or deployment appears in the window (count:1 in both the all-services and auth-service-scoped queries). The two changes are also temporally indistinguishable—they landed 60 seconds apart (14:00:00Z and 14:01:00Z)—so change history alone cannot attribute the 401s to one versus the other.

auth-service error_rate onset: error rate jumped from a ~0.2% baseline to 36% between 14:01 and 14:02 UTC. At 1-minute resolution, 14:01 shows avg 0.16% and 14:02 shows avg 36.08%, so the first-deviation timestamp is 2026-04-15T14:02:00Z.

The auth-service error rate is sustained and stable at ~35-37% from 14:02 through 15:56 (2h+), not spiking or decaying: e.g. max 40.33 at 15:08, values cluster 35-38. This is consistent with a consistent ~1/3 of validations failing rather than a total outage.

auth-service request_rate did NOT change at onset: it holds steady ~390-415 req/s across baseline and incident (14:00 400.07, 14:12 390.43, 14:28 417.5, up to 15:56 408.9). So the failing ~36% is a fraction of unchanged traffic, not a load surge.

auth-service latency_p99_ms did NOT change at onset: it stays flat ~85-101 ms throughout (baseline 14:00 = 89.29, onset 14:02 region 90.63, later 15:12 = 93.75 max 101.03). Failures are fast, so the 401 is likely returned without a slow downstream/backend dependency stall.

auth-service cpu_pct stayed flat ~34-42% (pre-onset 38.72 at 14:00, post-onset 38.41 at 14:12, mean 38.02) and rate_limited_per_min stayed flat ~2 req/min (mean 2.02), so the service is not CPU-saturated nor rate-limiting clients at onset.

api-gateway (upstream caller) shows the SAME onset but a LOWER magnitude: error_rate goes from <0.3% baseline to ~21% at the 14:00 bucket (avg 10.72, max 21.73) and stays ~21% through 15:56. The gateway 5xx (~21%) is lower than auth-service's 36%, indicating the gateway absorbs only a fraction of callers proportionally.

This confirms the identity namespace is partially unobservable, consistent with the reported log-pipeline outage — but no change-set item touches the pipeline, so the change history neither explains nor excludes it.

The entire record is: id cfg-2705, service auth-service, key jwt.signing.key_id, old_value k-2025-10, new_value k-2026-04, changed_at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z, author security-automation, description 'Scheduled signing-key rotation'.

No JWKS or key-distribution component exists in the service graph: querying the graph for 'jwks-service' fails with not_found, and the enumerated known_services list contains no JWKS, key-distribution, or KMS node (api-gateway, auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service, payment-service, settlement-service, notification-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db, user-db, redis-cache, kafka, exchange-api, bank-partner-api, kyc-provider, email-provider).

auth-service's only edges are to user-db (db), redis-cache (cache) and kyc-provider (external); api-gateway points at auth-service over http. There is no edge to any key-distribution/JWKS/pub-sub endpoint, so the propagation path by which k-2026-04 would reach replicas is not represented in the dependency graph.

Neither shared dependency exposes the requested metric names: redis-cache has no 'cache_hit_rate' (available: connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct) and user-db has no 'error_rate' (available: connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min). All redis-cache and user-db metrics measured (cache hit ratio, connected clients, CPU, DB connections, slow queries, replication lag) are stable across the entire 13:50-14:15Z window and show no deviation at the 14:00-14:02Z onset. This provides no support for H3 (a redis-cache or user-db degradation at 14:00Z invalidating a third of token checks) — the shared dependencies were healthy at the exact moment auth-service 401s began.

auth-service exposes a strictly closed set of 7 service-level metrics — cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts — with NO per-replica/pod dimension, NO pod-level error_rate breakdown, and NO JWKS/key-cache/key-fetch metric. The task's requested per-pod signal does not exist in this telemetry.

No pod/per-replica-scoped service identity resolves to auth-service; querying a pod-like service name fails with not_found and the enumerated known_services list contains only whole services (auth-service, api-gateway, redis-cache, ...), confirming there is no pod-level granularity to query.

auth-service 'restarts' is exactly 0.0 at every data point across the full pre-incident and incident window (10:00Z through 15:55Z, 241+ points at multiple resolutions, missing_points 0) — so no auth-service pod restarted around the 14:00-14:05Z onset. H1's mechanism (a pod loading the JWKS on startup and lagging key-id propagation) has no supporting restart signal.

The onset jump is captured at 1-minute resolution: auth-service error_rate goes 0.26 (14:00Z) -> 0.16 (14:01Z) -> 36.08 (14:02Z) -> 38.34 (14:03Z), i.e. a clean step from ~0.2% to ~36-38% between 14:01 and 14:02, not a gradual ramp.

Because telemetry offers only an aggregate service-level error_rate (no per-pod, no per-key/per-issuer/per-client grouping), the metric layer cannot distinguish H1's bimodal split (1/3 of pods high, 2/3 near zero) from H2's uniform ~36% regression. Statement is a limit of the data, not a positive result for either hypothesis.
